email.body1:
Tylinn, saw Prokeep stacked new integrations with FieldPulse and Dispatch and now powers 8,500-plus distributor locations.

That kind of expansion usually surfaces more accounts than the team can work before reps are stretched, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Prokeep off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Tylinn, quick follow-up for Prokeep.

As the platform and integrations grow, demand often outpaces coverage, and most teams cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit target this quarter. So the gap shows up late, and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Prokeep needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Tylinn, last bit of proof for Prokeep.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Prokeep's reply rate likely compares to other distribution-software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Tylinn, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority while you roll out the new integrations, no problem at all. Timing matters during a growth push, and I know it keeps an enablement team busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Prokeep either way.
